subtopics.title: Reading the Table Before You Draw

questions.question: In the schedule, quantity demanded falls from 100 to 20 as price rises from R2 to R10. This pattern reflects:
Why should you inspect the table before drawing anything?
options: To find which column has bigger numbers
To predict each curve's slope, spot the equal row, and choose sensible axis scales
Because tables are marked separately from graphs

questions.question: At which price do the demand and supply columns show the same quantity?

subtopics.title: Axes, Scales and Plotting the Points

questions.question: By convention, economics graphs place:
options: Price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis
Quantity on the vertical axis and price on the horizontal axis
Both variables on the same axis
Whichever variable is larger on the vertical axis

questions.question: What is wrong with an axis where the gap from 20 to 60 takes one block but 60 to 80 takes three blocks?
options: Nothing, as long as all values appear
The uneven scale bends the curves and makes every reading unreliable
It only matters for the demand curve

questions.question: The point for the demand row 'price R4, quantity 80' is plotted by:
options: Going up to 4 on the price axis and across to 80 on the quantity axis
Going up to 80 on the price axis and across to 4
Marking 4 and 80 both on the horizontal axis

questions.question: Which labels must appear for full presentation marks?
options: Only the curve names D and S
Axis labels with units, curve labels, and a heading
Labels are optional if the drawing is neat

questions.question: The equilibrium in our example is at:
Your curves cross at a price where the table's demand and supply columns are NOT equal. What does this mean?
options: At least one point was plotted incorrectly — check each point against its row

questions.question: What do the dotted lines from the intersection to each axis show?
options: The equilibrium price and quantity being read off the axes

subtopics.title: Reading Off Excess Supply at R8

questions.question: At R8, quantity demanded is 40 and quantity supplied is 80. The excess supply is:
On the graph, excess supply at R8 appears as:
options: The vertical distance between the curves at quantity 40
The horizontal distance between the demand and supply curves at the height of R8
The area under the supply curve
The distance from R6 to R8 on the price axis

questions.question: Why does a surplus occur at R8 specifically?
options: Because R8 is above the equilibrium price of R6, encouraging sellers while pricing out buyers
Because demand shifted left at R8

questions.question: The most common error when reading excess supply or demand off a graph is:
options: Reading the two quantities at different prices instead of along one horizontal line
Choosing a price on the vertical axis

questions.question: "The table is the boss" means:
options: When graph and table disagree, the table decides — the graph is just its portrait and invents nothing

questions.question: Interrogating the columns BEFORE drawing lets you:
options: Know what the finished picture MUST look like — and catch your own errors, like a demand line coming out uphill

questions.question: The special row to circle in your head is:
options: The first row of the table
The row with the biggest quantity
R6, where both columns say 60 — the lines must cross exactly there
The row with the highest price

questions.question: The subject's "handshake" for axes is:
options: Price UP the side, quantity ALONG the bottom — always
Quantity up the side, price along the bottom
Either way, as long as it's labelled

questions.question: Uneven scale steps are forbidden because:
options: They BEND lines that should be straight — and a bent line lies when you read from it, like a ruler with squashed centimetres
They make the graph too large

questions.question: Plotting as "postal work" means:
options: Posting the graph to the marker
Drawing the lines before the dots
Each table row is an address — up to the price, across to the quantity, drop a dot; the laws then draw the picture themselves

questions.question: Labels — Price (R), Quantity, title, D and S — are:
options: Free marks sitting on the table — markers award them directly

questions.question: The "level flight" at R8 touches:
options: Demand at 40 and supply at 80 — same height, two readings, gap of 40 units of excess supply

questions.question: The classic reading error is:
options: A crooked finger — reading the two curves at DIFFERENT heights instead of both readings on one price level

questions.question: At R4 the machine reads:
options: Supply 40, demand 80 — excess DEMAND of 40 units: below the resting place, buyers outrun sellers

questions.question: The skill is "routine, not talent" because:
options: Table interrogated, frame built, dots posted, level flights flown — every step is learnable by anyone willing to draw five graphs
